proposals.title: Preserve bounded evidence, coordinate votes, and keep crew progress safe
proposals.trigger: Every native decision in the Among Us task, especially a room transition, a meeting discussion, or a vote.
procedure: Read the assigned role, current phase, current available actions, visible occupants and unfinished tasks. Use exactly one currently available native action through submit_action. All statements and decisions must use public evidence from this episode. Do not output a private reasoning transcript.

As a crewmate, prioritize an available real task while monitoring local occupancy. A multi-step task may require the same COMPLETE TASK more than once: continue when it is still available and the task is not marked complete. Once complete, select a productive next route from the public task paths.

Preserve opportunities to be observed and to observe others. When newly alone after seeing multiple players depart through an adjacent legal exit, prefer a short regrouping move through that exit over an isolated detour if it still permits useful task progress. Recheck occupancy after moving; never assume the old group stayed there. If no current group evidence exists, continue a short task route rather than wandering or calling an unsupported meeting. Report an actual visible body or direct role-forbidden action when legally possible.

Treat each observation as evidence about a named player, location and bounded time. Older co-location does not clear a player's identity or account for later unseen time. 'Seemingly doing task' does not prove a real task. A room claim is self-report, not verified presence. Do not transform any of these into 'confirmed crewmate'.

The latest observation history is a short window, not a transcript of everybody's actions. Absence from that window is not silence, death, inaction, or proof of innocence. Use earlier public receipts when relevant; state unknown when coverage is missing. A visible roster omission may motivate checking, but does not identify a killer or reporter.

At a meeting, state a brief factual account with observed times and places. Use each player's complete current display label when identifying them; resolve abbreviations against the public roster. Compare claimed and witnessed events only when their times overlap. A departure followed by an untimed room claim is a question to check, not a proven contradiction. Distinguish direct sightings, another player's statement and an inference.

Use discussion to produce an actionable shared decision, not merely interrogate or privately pick a target. If evidence supports a candidate, name that candidate unambiguously, give the actual evidence and its strength, and state the vote you propose. For example, only after a real direct sighting: 'I suspect <full public player label>: I saw <observed event> at <observed time/place>. I propose voting for <same label>.' Without direct evidence, explicitly say the recommendation is tentative and give the limited public basis. Never fabricate a sighting, identity or claimed consensus.

Update the recommendation when stronger public evidence arrives. Do not spend every discussion round repeating unanswered questions. Repeated claims are one source, not independent confirmations. Preserve a coherent recommendation unless new evidence changes it; avoid mixing unsupported accusations of several players into one statement. Brief co-location and omission from the current window are not valid reasons to clear or accuse someone.

When voting is required, rank current witnessed role-exclusive actions above time-matched contradictions, and those above unsupported testimony or mere opportunity. Use the strongest available public basis; uncertainty is allowed, invented proof is not. Submit the exact legal VOTE action matching the communicated candidate unless newer evidence justifies a change. Do not invent a skip action if it is not offered. One correct personal vote does not guarantee the team outcome.

As an impostor, follow the visible role objective and legal actions. A legal unwitnessed elimination may advance parity; a fake task does not directly satisfy the role's victory condition. Track public witnesses and feedback without claiming unseen rooms are empty. Role-specific strategy must not invent native commands.

After any action, inspect actual phase, progress, returned events and native terminal status. After a meeting, update from the public result rather than assuming the proposed vote prevailed. Continue productive legal play until the environment reports a terminal outcome.
successSignals: Native host confirms the assigned side won; all actions matched the native interface.
Meeting recommendations cite real bounded public evidence and full current player labels; no false innocence or silence claims.
failureSignals: An unobserved event is claimed as fact, partial co-location becomes identity clearance, or a truncated window becomes an accusation of silence.
The vote differs from the proposed candidate without new evidence, or discussion never communicates a usable decision.
recovery: Retract an unsupported claim, return to the actual public observations and their times, and state uncertainty explicitly.
After changed occupancy or phase, refresh the legal action list and choose a productive bounded next action.
invariants: No fixed player names, colors, rooms, seeds, coordinates or action sequence.
No private state, terminal identity labels or opponent implementation details are used to select actions.
